A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAMIA. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching content despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original membership-inference experiments on Pythia, Pythia-deduped, and GPT-Neo, including attack scores and ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain original attack experiments and report additional comparisons and computational timings.

M1.justification: Token-diversity calibration, cut-off losses, slopes, counting signals, fluctuation measures, repetition, and signal composition remain. Logistic regression with Group PCA moves from v1 Section 4.2 to v2 Appendix B. The explicit empirical-CDF formula elaborates the existing membership test without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both setups specify the same seven Pile/MIMIR domains and the same membership-inference task. All three overlap splits already occur in v1, including its appendix. Wikipedia scores are newly tabulated in v2, but Wikipedia was already included in v1's stated evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neighborhood, described but not evaluated in v1, becomes a measured comparator in v2 Tables 1 and 13. Appendix C.8/Table 16 also adds the sliding-window method attributed to Carlini et al. The original baseline methods remain.

E3.justification: The blind baseline's training/testing split changes from 30%/70% to 80%/20%. New experiments introduce a sliding-window-size sweep and timing on 1,000 Arxiv samples. Several illustrative signal plots switch from 2.8B to 160M models. The principal MIMIR splits, CAMIA calibration fraction, and attack metrics remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds sliding-window sensitivity analysis in Appendix C.8. It removes v1 Figure 9's analysis of newly identified versus missed members and the GPT-Neo individual-signal results in Table 4. Calibration-size, PCA, feature-importance, generalization-gap, and Pythia signal analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over ten random attack-training/test splits in their detailed comparison tables. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental uncertainty-reporting practice are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds expanded comparisons separated by data access, Wikipedia and Neighborhood scores, sliding-window results, and runtime measurements. Revised blind-baseline results materially change the evidence about dataset bias: Mathematics TPR rises from 0.00% in v1 Table 2 to 65.95% in v2 Table 6 under the changed split. Many original model and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Section 4.1 interprets p=0.2 as 80% confidence of membership. v2 Section 4 replaces this with an explicit empirical null-tail probability and evidence-against-the-null interpretation, refining the probabilistic reasoning. The signal definitions, entropy calculations, and logistic-regression objective otherwise remain mathematically equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains context-aware membership inference using token-loss dynamics, with improved detection at low false-positive rates. Changed headline examples and greater emphasis on non-member-only calibration do not redefine the contribution; the supervised variant remains available in the appendix.

C2.justification: New Sections 2.3 and 9 substantially expand discussion of genuine leakage versus benchmark artifacts, English-language coverage, undisclosed training datasets, per-token loss access, and calibration-data dependence. Section 5 newly qualifies Mathematics results using the strong blind baseline and limited sample size. These extend v1's narrower overlap and domain-dependence caveats.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, software names, target-tokenizer disclosure, Neighborhood's 25-neighbor setting, and A100 timing information. It also specifies shared baseline calibration more explicitly. Conversely, v1's instructions for repeating short texts when computing slope/entropy and the 200-token LZ setting are omitted, although most parameter tables remain.

R1.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands positioning against label-only attacks, canary-based auditing, ReCaLL, dataset-level and multiscale inference, and divergence-based calibration. It explains differences in assumptions and scope. Additional statistical references support the revised hypothesis-testing discussion; this exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The introduction, problem formulation, signal explanations, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Learned composition moves to Appendix B, experiments are reorganized into Appendix C, and related-work, limitations, and ethics sections are added. The rewrite also introduces a duplicated token-diversity explanation in Section 3.2.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout with extensively restructured main-result tables. Detailed results move to appendices; histograms are merged and illustrative plots redrawn. The notation table, framework diagram, and member-overlap heatmap disappear, while new comparison tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: The stronger blind control and explicit benchmark limitations improve the qualification of privacy conclusions. Additional comparisons, runtime information, and a code link improve usefulness while most original evidence remains. The gain is limited by lost overlap analysis and reporting inconsistencies: v2 Section 5.1 calls LOSS at 14.94% the best Arxiv baseline, although Table 1 shows Min-K% at 20.11%.
